problems.comment:
Large quantities of fresh snow and the wind-drifted snow are prone to triggering. Single winter sport participants can release avalanches easily. Natural avalanches are possible, even large ones. 
 Backcountry touring calls for great caution and restraint.
On grassy slopes numerous small and, in isolated cases, medium-sized gliding avalanches are to be expected. Caution is to be exercised in areas with glide cracks.

bulletin.snowpack: With intense snowfall and a strong westerly wind, wind slabs prone to triggering are forming. In addition, the snow layers from last week are in some cases still prone to triggering. Pronounced faceted weak layers are scarcely present.
bulletin.tendency:
Dry avalanches
The danger of dry avalanches will gradually decrease. Even single winter sport participants can release avalanches as before. Backcountry touring and other off-piste activities call for experience in the assessment of avalanche danger and caution.
Wet-snow avalanches
Numerous gliding avalanches are to be expected. Caution is to be exercised in areas with glide cracks.

problems.comment:
Large quantities of fresh snow and the wind-drifted snow are prone to triggering. Natural avalanches are to be expected. They can be released in the new snow and wind slab layers. In very isolated cases avalanches can also be triggered in the old snowpack, especially on north and east facing slopes above approximately 2600 m. In the typical avalanche paths the avalanches can in isolated cases reach very large size and endanger transportation routes situated at relatively high altitudes. 
 The conditions are very critical for backcountry touring.
On steep grassy slopes numerous gliding avalanches are to be expected, even large ones in isolated cases. Caution is to be exercised in areas with glide cracks.

bulletin.snowpack:
Large amounts of new snow and wind drifted snow are being deposited on thick snow layers from the past week. Avalanches can be triggered both in the new snow layers and in the already somewhat older snow layers.
On north- and east-facing slopes above around 2600 m there is in places coarse-grained old snow at the snow base. This old snow near the ground is now overlain by such a thick layer that fractures in layers of the snowpack near the ground are not very likely.
bulletin.tendency:
Dry avalanches
The danger of dry avalanches will decrease. However, single winter sports participants can still release avalanches. Backcountry touring and other off-piste activities call for experience in the assessment of avalanche danger and caution.
Wet-snow avalanches
Numerous gliding avalanches are to be expected. Caution is to be exercised in areas with glide cracks.
